recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce code.coding slicing solely to match the old tracker wording unless the work group intentionally reverses the current patternCodeableConcept representation.
issue_request: FHIR-13964 asked to add system as a discriminator for code slicing in the vital signs profiles, following a BodyTemp discussion where code-only slicing could collide if different code systems reuse the same code value.
initial_application: The issue was historically applied by git commit 1eb8db446d5aca682e107a14e5fbb3b4e22d606a, 'GF#13897, GF#13964, GF#14037 vitals profiles slicing', which changed the old source/observation/observation-vitalsigns-profile-spreadsheet.xml on 2018-02-23. No prior combined-branch Issue-Reconcile-Key: FHIR-13964 commit existed before this run.
additional_context: The current Observation vital signs IG references the active StructureDefinition resources for vitalsigns, vitalspanel, bp, bodytemp, bodyheight, bodyweight, bmi, headcircum, resprate, heartrate, and oxygensat. Current per-measurement profiles use patternCodeableConcept with http://loinc.org and the identifying LOINC code rather than the older STU3 code.coding slicing representation, and the narrative tells implementers to check whether the coding is present in the CodeableConcept. The referenced Zulip discussion explicitly treated discriminator-on-code-and-system as equivalent to a pattern CodeableConcept for this use. FHIR-13968 is an already-published related audit for adjacent vital-sign code inclusion wording.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because current source preserves the requested system+code semantics without needing source edits or a return to code.coding slicing.
